chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya al-Dahqan narrated to me. He said:

I was in Baghdad with the judge of Baghdad, whose name was Sama'a, when a man from the elders of Baghdad came to him and said: May Allah rectify the judge. I went on Hajj in past years and I passed through Kufa. During my return I entered its mosque. While I was standing in the mosque intending to pray, suddenly before me was a Bedouin woman with flowing locks of hair, wearing a woolen cloak, and she was calling out and saying:

O renowned one in the heavens! O renowned one in the Earths! O renowned one in the Hereafter! O renowned one in this world! The tyrants and kings strove to extinguish your light and suppress your remembrance, but Allah refused and willed only exaltation for your remembrance and only brightness and completion for your light, even if the polytheists were averse.

He said: So I said: O maidservant of Allah! Who is this that you describe with this description? She said: That is Amir al-Mu'minin. He said: So I said to her: Which commander of the faithful is he? She said: Ali ibn Abi Talib, through whom and through whose wilaya alone tawhid is valid. He said: So I turned toward her, and I did not see anyone.

key_terms.إِطْفَاء النُّور: Extinguishing the light — a metaphor for attempts to suppress the Imam's authority
key_terms.التَّوْحِيد: Tawhid — divine unity, here linked inseparably to wilayat Ali
key_terms.الْوِلَايَة: Wilaya — guardianship, authority, the special bond between the Imam and his followers
key_terms.مَشْهُور: Renowned, widely known — applied here to Ali in both the cosmic and earthly realms

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the mysterious Bedouin woman praising Imam Ali in Kufa mosque?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq (d. 381 AH) narrates a mysterious encounter in the mosque of Kufa, where a Bedouin woman is heard praising Imam Ali (peace be upon him) with cosmic epithets — describing him as renowned in the heavens and the earth — and declaring that tawhid is not complete without his wilaya (guardianship). The woman vanishes after her declaration, suggesting a supernatural or angelic nature, which is a common motif in Shia devotional literature to underscore the transcendent status of the Imams. This hadith addresses the Shia theological doctrine that wilayat Ali is an integral component of monotheistic faith, and it was transmitted during the period of the Lesser Occultation (260-329 AH) when questions of legitimate leadership were especially pressing for the Shia community.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Jarir al-Tabari narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan b. Muhammad narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan b. Yahya al-Dahqan narrated to me. He said:

I was in Baghdad with the judge of Baghdad, and his name was Sama`a. A man from the elders of Baghdad visited him and said to him: May Allah rectify the judge. I went on Hajj in one of the past years and I passed through Kufa. I entered its mosque. I stood in the mosque intending to pray when I saw a Bedouin woman before me ... with a blanket over her. She was calling out and saying:

O he who is prominent in the heavens! O he who is prominent in the Earths! O he who is prominent in the Hereafter! O he who is prominent in this world! The tyrants and the kings strived to extinguish your light and suppress your remembrance, but Allah refused and exalted your remembrance and illuminated and perfected your light, even if the pagans may be averse.

He said: So, I said: O maidservant of Allah! Who is this that you describe with this description? She said: That is Amir al-Mu’minin. He said: So, I said: Which commander of the faithful is he? She said: `Ali b. Abi Talib, without whose wilaya there cannot be monotheism. He said: So, I turned to her, and I did not see anyone.
